title: Modi Greets Nation on Diwali Eve, Says He Will Celebrate With Soldiers Again
excerpt: In a video message on Saturday, the Prime Minister wished the country happiness and prosperity and confirmed he will keep up his annual Diwali tradition with defence personnel; the festival falls on Sunday, November 8.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings to the nation in a video message on Saturday, November 7, a day before the festival.
  • He said he will again celebrate Diwali with India's defence personnel, continuing the annual tradition he has kept throughout his time as prime minister.
  • Modi called the festival of lights a symbol of the country's pledge against darkness and wished citizens happiness, wellbeing and prosperity.
  • Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Earlier on Saturday, Modi exchanged greetings with Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan, who then travelled to Ayodhya for the Deepotsav celebrations.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday extended Diwali greetings to people across the country and said he would spend the festival with soldiers again this year, keeping up an annual tradition he has maintained since taking office — and that he traces back 25 years.

In a short video message titled "Have a great Diwali," posted on his social media accounts on the eve of the festival, Modi said the festival of lights symbolises the country's pledge against darkness.

"May this festival bring happiness, wellbeing and prosperity for all. Just like you all, I also celebrate this festival with enthusiasm. Like every year, I will again be celebrating Diwali with our brave defence personnel."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

A tradition kept every year

Modi has celebrated Diwali with members of the armed forces every year as prime minister, travelling to forward posts and military installations rather than spending the festival in New Delhi. Last Diwali, he marked the festival aboard the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant off the Goa coast, where he addressed naval personnel and spent the night on the ship. Earlier this year, speaking on Kargil Vijay Diwas, he noted that he has kept the practice of celebrating Diwali at the border with soldiers for 25 years, going back to his time before national office.

The Prime Minister's announcement did not say where this year's celebration with defence personnel will take place. Such visits are typically confirmed only shortly before or after they happen.

Greetings exchanged, Ayodhya lights up

Earlier on Saturday, Modi called on Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan at Uprashtrapati Bhawan in New Delhi, where the two exchanged Diwali greetings. Radhakrishnan subsequently travelled to Ayodhya to take part in Deepotsav 2026, the Uttar Pradesh government's festival-eve celebration on the banks of the Saryu, which this year marks its tenth edition. Our coverage of tonight's Deepotsav in Ayodhya has the details of the planned lamp-lighting across 56 ghats.

Modi had earlier in the week extended wishes on Dhanteras, which opens the five-day Diwali period. The festival period runs through Bhai Dooj on Tuesday — our guide to the five days of Diwali 2026 sets out what each day marks.

Why it matters

The Diwali-with-soldiers visit has become one of the fixed rituals of Modi's premiership, intended as a gesture toward personnel who spend the country's biggest festival on duty away from their families. This year's message also carried a line for the home front: in the same spirit, our story of a Kargil officer who promised to come home "next Diwali" recalls what the festival means to soldiers' families.

Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, with Lakshmi Puja performed in the evening.
